approaches.name: Three nested loops with a set
approaches.intuition: Try every triple of positions and collect the zero-sum ones in a set of sorted tuples to remove duplicates.
steps: Sort each zero-sum triple and store it in a set
Sort the set for the output

approaches.name: Sort, then two pointers
approaches.intuition: Sorting lets you walk two pointers towards each other for every fixed first number, and equal neighbours are skipped instead of stored.
steps: Skip repeated values at all three positions
approaches.space: O(1) besides the output and the sort
pitfalls: Skipping duplicates after a hit, not before checking it: the first copy must still be used.
Use positions, not values, so three different positions are guaranteed.
The output order is lexicographic: sorted input produces it directly.

talkTrackMd: Reduce 3Sum to 2Sum on a sorted array, then explain duplicate skipping at each level. Quote O(n^2) and note that this is optimal for the general problem.
